title: "Compare GMFRM probability surfaces"

  rmarkdown::html_document:
    self_contained: true

vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Compare GMFRM probability surfaces}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

How likely is a particular score if the same performance is rated by someone
else or on a different criterion? Select a rater, a criterion and a score
event in each panel. Compare the dark lines for the **fitted raters**. The
surface shows what the model predicts if that rater's severity changes by up
to one logit, holding discrimination, criterion difficulty and steps fixed.
Both horizontal axes are in logits. A positive change represents a more severe rater.

```{css, echo=FALSE}
.main-container { max-width: 1120px !important; }
.surface-pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 305px), 1fr)); gap: 12px; margin: 1em 0; }
.surface-panel { min-width: 0; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid #c9d5db; border-radius: 6px; background: white; color: #20323a; }
.surface-controls { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px 10px; }
.surface-controls label { display: grid; gap: 3px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; }
.surface-controls select { font: inherit; font-weight: 400; color: #20323a; border: 1px solid #869ba6; border-radius: 3px; background: white; padding: 3px 5px; }
.surface-readout { display: block; color: #193e4d; font-size: 14px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```{r surface-data, include=FALSE}
library(mfrmr)
fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "measurement-fits.rds", package = "mfrmr"))$gpcm
stopifnot(summary(fit)$readiness$ready, identical(unique(fit$slopes[["Formula"]]), "full_predictor"))
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
raters <- sort(unique(as.character(ratings$Rater)))
criteria <- sort(unique(as.character(ratings$Criterion)))
scores <- seq(fit$rating_min, fit$rating_max)

# Integer tenths give exact indices for theta - change on the shared grid.
ability10 <- -30:30
change10 <- -10:10
effective10 <- seq(min(ability10) - max(change10), max(ability10) - min(change10))
contexts <- expand.grid(Rater = raters, Criterion = criteria, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
prob <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(contexts)), function(i) {
  nd <- contexts[rep(i, length(effective10)), , drop = FALSE]
  p <- predict(fit, newdata = nd, theta = effective10 / 10, type = "probs")
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(p), as.character(scores)), all(is.finite(p)),
            max(abs(rowSums(p) - 1)) < 1e-10)
  unname(p)
})
event_labels <- c(paste("Score =", scores), paste("Score ≥", scores[-1]))
surface_data <- list(raters = raters, criteria = criteria, scores = scores,
                     ability10 = ability10, change10 = change10,
                     first = min(effective10), prob = prob)
```

```{r surface-panels, echo=FALSE}
surface_panel <- function(rater) {
  tags <- htmltools::tags
  control <- function(label, values, default) {
    tags$label(label, tags$select(lapply(values, function(v)
      tags$option(value = v, selected = if (v == default) "selected", v))))
  }
  scene <- list(xaxis = list(title = "Person ability", range = c(-3, 3), tickvals = c(-2, 0, 2)),
                yaxis = list(title = "Severity change", range = c(-1, 1), tickvals = c(-1, 0, 1)),
                zaxis = list(title = "Probability", range = c(0, 1), tickformat = ".0%"),
                camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.75, y = -1.95, z = 1.30)),
                aspectmode = "manual", aspectratio = list(x = 1.35, y = 1, z = 0.85))
  # Initialize with the default event and context. Menu changes reuse the same predictions.
  ci <- which(contexts$Rater == rater & contexts$Criterion == "Content")
  tail_prob <- rowSums(prob[[ci]][, scores >= 3, drop = FALSE])
  z <- t(vapply(change10, function(d)
    tail_prob[ability10 - d - min(effective10) + 1L], numeric(length(ability10))))
  g <- plotly::plot_ly(x = ability10 / 10, y = change10 / 10, z = z, type = "surface",
    colorscale = "Cividis", cmin = 0, cmax = 1, showscale = FALSE, opacity = 0.88,
    height = 355)
  g <- plotly::add_trace(g, inherit = FALSE, type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines",
    x = ability10 / 10, y = rep(0, length(ability10)), z = z[change10 == 0, ],
    showlegend = FALSE, line = list(color = "#192a3f", width = 7))
  g <- plotly::layout(g, scene = scene, margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, b = 31, t = 3),
                      hoverlabel = list(align = "left"), uirevision = "keep-camera")
  g <- plotly::config(g, displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE, scrollZoom = FALSE)
  g <- htmlwidgets::onRender(g, paste(readLines("probability-surfaces.js"), collapse = "\n"),
                             data = surface_data)
  tags$section(class = "surface-panel", `aria-label` = paste("Comparison panel, initially", rater),
    tags$div(class = "surface-controls", control("Rater", raters, rater),
      control("Criterion", criteria, "Content"), control("Score event", event_labels, "Score ≥ 3")),
    g, tags$output(class = "surface-readout", `aria-live` = "polite"))
}
htmltools::div(class = "surface-pair", surface_panel("R01"), surface_panel("R03"))
```

Both panels use the same ability, severity-change and probability scales.
Hover to read the probability at a point. Rotate either panel to change both viewing angles. To compare categories, set the
same rater and criterion on both sides and select different score events.
For this four-point rubric, “Score ≥ 3” adds the probabilities of scores 3 and 4.

### What the calculation holds fixed

The bundled synthetic GMFRM has rater-specific discrimination and
criterion-specific steps. On the dark line the severity change is zero, so the
probabilities come directly from the calibrated rater–criterion combination.
For this model, discrimination multiplies the full predictor. Increasing rater
severity by `d` logits therefore gives the same category probabilities as
predicting at `theta - d` in the original context. A GMFRM that applies
discrimination only to ability requires a different adjustment.

Differences between calibrated raters can reflect both severity and
discrimination. Differences between criteria can reflect difficulty and step
locations. The surfaces show conditional point predictions. To reproduce the
two default readouts at ability zero:

```{r surface-example}
library(mfrmr)
fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "measurement-fits.rds", package = "mfrmr"))$gpcm
ctx <- data.frame(Rater = c("R01", "R03"), Criterion = "Content")
p <- predict(fit, newdata = ctx, theta = 0, type = "probs")
data.frame(ctx, P_exactly_3 = p[, "3"], P_at_least_3 = rowSums(p[, c("3", "4")]))
```
